items.title: ICare-FASTER: point-of-care hs-troponin I cuts ED stay by 47 minutes in suspected MI with no rise in 30-day MI or cardiac death (Circulation)
items.summary: In a six-hospital New Zealand stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial of nearly 60,000 ED presentations, swapping central-lab hs-troponin for a whole-blood point-of-care hs-cTnI assay in the same accelerated rule-out pathway shortened ED length of stay by 13% (47 minutes) with identical 30-day safety (Than et al., Circulation, Oct 19, 2026).
bullets: Design: pragmatic stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial at 6 New Zealand hospitals, Feb 2023 to Jan 2025; 59,980 ED presentations (44,747 people, mean age 61, 49.5% women), 31,392 in the intervention phase.
Intervention: the same accelerated diagnostic pathway with a single-sample rule-out step, using a whole-blood point-of-care hs-cTnI assay instead of the central-laboratory hs-cTn assay.
Primary outcome: adjusted ED length of stay fell by 13% (95% CI 9-16%; P<0.001), about 47 minutes (95% CI 33-61) from a control mean of 376 minutes.
Safety: 30-day MI or cardiac death was 0.39% in both arms (P=0.54).
Context: described as the first evaluation of a point-of-care hs-cTnI strategy in routine care; it is a single-country pragmatic trial, so results depend on local pathways and lab turnaround times.
items.source: Than M, et al. ICare-FASTER. Circulation, Oct 19, 2026. doi:10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.126.080866
